guarantees.claim: For each share i, data_truncated[i] is assigned the lower KeyWidth bits of data_i[i].

uncertain_points.claim: The truncation of data_i[i] to lower KeyWidth bits discards any upper bits. It is unclear whether the discarded bits are expected to be zero or if they contain key material that should be preserved.
uncertain_points.cond: when upper bits of data_i[i] are non-zero
uncertain_points.risk: If the upper bits hold key entropy, discarding them weakens the key strength.

formal_sketch.antecedent: when upper bits of data_i[i] are non-zero
formal_sketch.consequent: The truncation of data_i[i] to lower KeyWidth bits discards any upper bits. It is unclear whether the discarded bits are expected to be zero or if they contain key material that should be preserved

security_implications: The truncation of data_i to lower KeyWidth bits may discard key entropy present in the upper bits, potentially weakening the key. If the upper bits are expected to be zero, this is safe; if they contain secret material, it is a security vulnerability. Requires cross-chunk verification to confirm data_i width matches KeyWidth or upper bits are masked.
